CYP450 substrate: inducers (rifampin, phenobarbital, phenytoin) ↓ effect; inhibitors (antibiotics, antifungals, SSRIs) ↑ effect

children.label: Antiplatelet Agents
children: Vascular injury exposes collagen/vWF → platelets bind via GP1b → activation → degranulation → releases ADP, serotonin, TXA2 → aggregation
ADP → P2Y12 receptor → aggregation
COX-1 (constitutive, in platelets) synthesizes TXA2 from arachidonic acid → vasoconstriction + aggregation
GP IIb/IIIa receptor binds fibrinogen → final common pathway of platelet aggregation
Drug(s): Aspirin | MOA: Irreversibly acetylates COX-1 & COX-2 | Notes / Key AE: "Pseudo-allergy" in asthma/nasal polyps (↑leukotrienes) → use ADP inhibitor instead
Drug(s): Clopidogrel, ticagrelor, prasugrel ("-grel") | MOA: Irreversible P2Y12 inhibitors | Notes / Key AE: Ticlopidine → neutropenia/granulocytopenia (2%) → monitor CBC
Drug(s): Abciximab | MOA: Monoclonal Ab blocking GP IIb/IIIa | Notes / Key AE: Thrombocytopenia
Drug(s): Eptifibatide, tirofiban | MOA: Block GP IIb/IIIa | Notes / Key AE: IV continuous infusion; thrombocytopenia
Drug(s): Dipyridamole, cilostazol | MOA: Phosphodiesterase inhibitors → ↑cAMP → ↓platelet function | Notes / Key AE: Cilostazol: vasodilator → treats claudication (PAD); risk of coronary steal

Uses: ↓ CV events in PAD/CAD (do not relieve claudication — cilostazol does); acute MI/ACS — give ASAP (chewable ASA in STEMI); dual antiplatelet therapy prevents stent thrombosis; prevents ischemic stroke in atherosclerosis
AE (general): ↑ bleeding time

children.label: Fibrinolytics
children: tPA & streptokinase convert plasminogen → plasmin → degrades fibrin clots
Prolong PT & PTT; D-dimer = fibrin degradation product (marker of clot lysis)
Uses: ischemic stroke (IV fibrinolytics within 3–4.5h of onset); severe acute DVT/PE; MI (PCI preferred in STEMI, ideally within ~2h)
AE: hemorrhagic stroke (main risk)
CI: recent head trauma/intracranial surgery, hemorrhage on CT, severe hypertension
Streptokinase: unique risk of allergic reaction/anaphylaxis
Reversal: aminocaproic acid (inhibits plasminogen activation), tranexamic acid (reverses tPA), FFP/cryoprecipitate (reverse coagulopathy)

children.label: Antimetabolites
children: Physiology: dUMP → dTMP via thymidylate synthase (THF donates carbon → becomes DHF); DHFR regenerates DHF → THF

children.label: Antimetabolites › Methotrexate (MTX)
children: MOA: inhibits DHFR → ↓ THF regeneration → ↓ thymidine synthesis → blocks DNA/RNA synthesis (S phase)
Uses: leukemia/lymphoma; ectopic pregnancy/abortifacient (± misoprostol); molar pregnancy/choriocarcinoma; psoriasis; 1st-line DMARD for RA; immunosuppression (IBD, SLE, vasculitis, dermatomyositis)
AE: folate deficiency, megaloblastic anemia, pancytopenia/myelosuppression, ↑infection risk, pulmonary fibrosis, hepatotoxicity (monitor LFTs), alopecia, mucositis
Antidote: leucovorin (folinic acid)

children.label: Antimetabolites › 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU)
children: MOA: complexes with THF → inhibits thymidylate synthase → ↓ thymidine production
AE: diarrhea, photosensitivity/rash, myelosuppression, ↑infection risk — no antidote

children.label: Antimetabolites › Hydroxyurea
children: MOA: inhibits ribonucleotide reductase (UDP → dUDP) → blocks thymidine synthesis
Use: sickle cell disease (↑ HbF → protects against HbS polymerization)
AE: myelosuppression, ↑infection risk

children.label: Antimetabolites › Purine Analogs
children: Physiology: PRPP → IMP → AMP & GMP
Azathioprine = prodrug of 6-mercaptopurine (6-MP); activated by HGPRT → blocks IMP synthesis → inhibits DNA synthesis (S phase)
Uses: hematologic malignancy (ALL); immunosuppression (SLE, transplant); RA (DMARD); IBD
AE: bone marrow suppression, ↑infection (monitor CBCs), pancreatitis, hepatotoxicity
Allopurinol (xanthine oxidase inhibitor) → ↑ 6-MP levels → toxicity (key drug interaction)
Mycophenolate mofetil: inhibits IMP dehydrogenase → ↓GMP synthesis → ↓lymphocyte proliferation; used for transplant/SLE/myasthenia gravis, RA; AE: GI effects, immunosuppression/infection
Cladribine: purine analog → treats hairy cell leukemia; AE: immunosuppression

children.label: Antimetabolites › Cytarabine & Gemcitabine (Pyrimidine Analogs)
children: MOA: inhibit DNA polymerase; block S phase
Cytarabine: hematologic malignancies only (AML, NHL)
Gemcitabine: hematologic and solid tumors
AE: myelosuppression, ↑infection risk

children.label: Antitumor Antibiotics › Bleomycin
children: MOA: binds DNA → generates free radicals → single/double-strand DNA breaks; blocks G2 phase
Uses: Hodgkin/non-Hodgkin lymphoma, germ cell tumors, SCC (skin, cervix, vulva)
AE: pulmonary toxicity (pneumonitis, infiltrates) — hallmark; skin toxicity; mucositis/stomatitis; alopecia

children.label: Antitumor Antibiotics › Anthracyclines — "-rubicin" (doxorubicin, daunorubicin)
children: MOA: generate free radicals + intercalate DNA → block DNA/RNA synthesis
Uses: broad range of solid & hematologic malignancies
AE: cardiotoxicity (dilated cardiomyopathy) — dose-limiting; myelosuppression; mucositis; alopecia
Dexrazoxane (iron chelator) prevents anthracycline cardiotoxicity

children.label: Antitumor Antibiotics › Actinomycin D
children: MOA: intercalates DNA → blocks DNA/RNA synthesis
Uses: pediatric tumors (Wilms tumor, Ewing sarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma)
AE: alopecia, myelosuppression

children.label: Alkylating Agents
children: General MOA: donate alkyl group → DNA cross-links (cell-cycle nonspecific)

children.label: Alkylating Agents › Cyclophosphamide
children: Activated by hepatic CYP450
Uses: leukemia/lymphoma, breast/ovarian cancer; immunosuppression (nephrotic syndrome, vasculitis, autoimmune hemolytic anemia)
AE: myelosuppression; hemorrhagic cystitis (prevented by MESNA); ↑ bladder cancer risk; SIADH → hyponatremia; infertility/premature menopause

children.label: Alkylating Agents › Busulfan
children: Use: conditioning agent prior to bone marrow transplant
AE: lung toxicity (interstitial fibrosis, alveolar hemorrhage); hyperpigmentation ("busulfan tan")

children.label: Alkylating Agents › Nitrosoureas — "-mustine" (carmustine, lomustine); streptozotocin
children: Highly lipophilic → cross BBB → treat brain tumors (glioblastoma multiforme)
AE: neurotoxicity (convulsions, dizziness, ataxia)

children.label: Microtubule Inhibitors › Vinca Alkaloids — vincristine, vinblastine
children: MOA: inhibit microtubule formation/mitotic spindle assembly; block M phase
Uses: leukemia, lymphoma, pediatric tumors, breast cancer, germ cell cancer
AE: vincristine → peripheral sensory neuropathy, autonomic dysfunction (paralytic ileus, constipation); alopecia; myelosuppression (esp. vinblastine)

children.label: Microtubule Inhibitors › Taxanes — paclitaxel, docetaxel, cabazitaxel
children: MOA: stabilize microtubules, prevent degradation → improper spindle function; block M phase
AE: alopecia, peripheral neuropathy, myelosuppression

children.label: Platinum Analogs — cisplatin, carboplatin, oxaliplatin
children: MOA: bind DNA → intrastrand/interstrand cross-links
Uses: NSCLC, SCLC, testicular, ovarian, bladder cancer

AE: ototoxicity (hearing loss, tinnitus — esp. cisplatin); neurotoxicity (peripheral neuropathy — esp. cisplatin); nephrotoxicity/ATN (muddy brown casts — esp. cisplatin); myelosuppression/immunosuppression (esp. carboplatin)
Prevention: amifostine (free radical scavenger) + IV saline diuresis → prevent cisplatin nephrotoxicity

children.label: Topoisomerase Inhibitors › Topo II Inhibitors — etoposide, teniposide
children: MOA: double-strand breaks, prevent religation → block S & G2 phase
Uses: testicular cancer, SCLC, Hodgkin/non-Hodgkin lymphoma
AE: myelosuppression, immunosuppression, alopecia

children.label: Topoisomerase Inhibitors › Topo I Inhibitors — topotecan, irinotecan
children: MOA: single-strand nick to relieve DNA supercoiling
Uses: topotecan → ovarian cancer, SCLC; irinotecan → colon cancer
AE: myelosuppression, severe diarrhea

children.label: Targeted Therapy › Small-Molecule Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors
children: Drug: Imatinib | Target: BCR-ABL (Philadelphia chr., t(9;22)); also c-kit | Main Use: CML; GIST (c-kit) | Key AE: Fluid retention (ankle/periorbital edema)
Drug: Erlotinib | Target: EGFR | Main Use: NSCLC (EGFR overexpression) | Key AE: Acneiform rash, diarrhea
Drug: Sunitinib, sorafenib | Target: VEGFR | Main Use: Renal cell carcinoma | Key AE: Hyperkeratosis/skin rash, ↑hemorrhage risk
Drug: Vemurafenib | Target: B-Raf kinase | Main Use: BRAF V600E+ melanoma | Key AE: —

children.label: Targeted Therapy › Monoclonal Antibodies
children: Drug: Rituximab | Target: CD20 (B cells) | Main Use: CLL; RA (DMARD); microscopic polyangiitis/Wegener's | Key AE: Immunosuppression/infection, ↑PML risk
Drug: Cetuximab | Target: EGFR | Main Use: Colorectal cancer, SCC | Key AE: Acneiform rash
Drug: Bevacizumab | Target: VEGF | Main Use: Metastatic colorectal/SCC; wet macular degeneration | Key AE: Bleeding, ↑thrombosis, GI perforation
Drug: Alemtuzumab | Target: CD52 (B & T cells) | Main Use: CLL | Key AE: —
Drug: Trastuzumab | Target: HER2 | Main Use: HER2+ breast cancer | Key AE: Cardiotoxicity (↓LVEF, heart failure)
General mAb AE: infusion reactions (headache, fever, rash, pruritus, dyspnea, hypotension)
Chimeric antibodies (rituximab, rarely cetuximab) → serum sickness (fever, rash, arthralgia, 7–10 days post-infusion)

children.label: Arachidonic Acid Pathway
children: Phospholipase A2 (PLA2) → releases arachidonic acid from the cell membrane
COX-1 → constitutively expressed (most cells); COX-2 → induced by inflammation
COX-1 → synthesizes TXA2 (vasoconstriction, platelet aggregation) + gastric cytoprotective prostaglandins
COX-2 → in vascular endothelium/smooth muscle; synthesizes PGI2 (prostacyclin) → vasodilation, inhibits platelet aggregation
COX-1 AND COX-2 → dilate the afferent arteriole (maintain GFR)
COX-2 → also ↑ vascular permeability, ↑ pain sensitivity, induces fever

children.label: NSAIDs (General) — Diclofenac, Ketorolac, Indomethacin, Meloxicam, Piroxicam, Naproxen
children: MOA → reversible inhibition of COX-1 AND COX-2
Indomethacin → closes the ductus arteriosus
AE (COX-1) → gastric inflammation/erosion/ulceration, GI bleeding, ↑ bleeding time
AE (renal) → ↑ BP (↓ Na+ excretion); acute interstitial nephritis; afferent arteriole constriction → ↓ GFR (worsened with ACE inhibitors); renal papillary necrosis
AE → ↑ serum lithium; aplastic anemia (esp. indomethacin); ↓ renin → hypoaldosteronism → hyperkalemia (type IV RTA)
Avoid in patients at risk for AKI, MI, or ↓ renal perfusion
Avoid in 3rd trimester → premature closure of ductus arteriosus (highest risk: indomethacin, ibuprofen)

children.label: Aspirin
children: MOA → irreversible acetylation of COX-1 AND COX-2
Uses → Kawasaki disease (most common childhood vasculitis: fever, conjunctivitis, oral/lip erythema, rash, cervical lymphadenopathy)
Reye syndrome → aspirin + viral illness in children → rapidly progressive encephalopathy (confusion, seizure, coma) + hepatic dysfunction (steatosis, hepatomegaly)
Toxicity → respiratory alkalosis first, then anion gap metabolic acidosis; tinnitus
Toxicity treatment → activated charcoal; serum/urine alkalinization (sodium bicarbonate) → ↑ renal excretion, pulls aspirin out of CNS

children.label: Celecoxib
children: Selective COX-2 inhibitor → ↓ ulcer/bleeding risk (spares COX-1)
AE → ↑ risk of ischemic cardiovascular disease — avoid in acute MI, stable angina
Is a sulfa drug

children.label: Acetaminophen
children: MOA → inhibits COX-2 → antipyretic + analgesic (NOT anti-inflammatory)
Uses → mild-moderate pain, osteoarthritis, some RA
Toxic metabolite NAPQI depletes hepatic glutathione → hepatotoxicity
Treatment → activated charcoal (acute); N-acetylcysteine (restores glutathione)

children.label: Overview
children: Purine metabolism → hypoxanthine → (xanthine oxidase) → xanthine → (xanthine oxidase) → uric acid

children.label: Acute Gout / Pseudogout
children: Classic presentation → 1st metatarsal joint
Treatment → NSAIDs (indomethacin, 1st-line); glucocorticoids (prednisone); colchicine (oral, within 12–24h)
Colchicine → binds intracellular tubulin → prevents microtubule polymerization → disrupts neutrophil migration/phagocytosis/degranulation; AE → diarrhea
Pseudogout → same acute treatment; crystals: positively birefringent, rhomboid-shaped

children.label: Chronic Gout
children: Allopurinol, Febuxostat → inhibit xanthine oxidase
Allopurinol AE → mild rash, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, DRESS; ↑ toxicity of purine analogs (6-mercaptopurine, azathioprine)
Probenecid (uricosuric) → ↓ renal tubular reabsorption of uric acid; only for under-excretors; AE → ↑ renal stone risk; inhibits excretion of many drugs (e.g., penicillin); is a sulfa drug
Aspirin → high dose is uricosuric (↓ reabsorption); low dose ↑ retention (inhibits excretion) — paradoxical dose effect
Pegloticase (recombinant uricase) → converts uric acid → water-soluble allantoin; IV; AE → hemolysis in G6PD deficiency, anaphylaxis
Tumor lysis syndrome → uric acid crystals after cytotoxic chemo (esp. lymphoma, ALL) — prevent with allopurinol
Lesch-Nyhan syndrome → hyperuricemia (self-mutilation/lip-biting) → managed with allopurinol
Drug(s): NSAIDs, glucocorticoids, colchicine | Phase: Acute | MOA: Anti-inflammatory; colchicine → ↓ microtubule polymerization | Key Note: Colchicine → diarrhea
Drug(s): Allopurinol, febuxostat | Phase: Chronic | MOA: ↓ xanthine oxidase | Key Note: SJS/DRESS; ↑ 6-MP/azathioprine toxicity
Drug(s): Probenecid | Phase: Chronic (under-excretors) | MOA: ↑ uric acid excretion | Key Note: Sulfa drug; ↓ penicillin excretion
Drug(s): Pegloticase | Phase: Chronic | MOA: Uricase → allantoin | Key Note: G6PD hemolysis, anaphylaxis; IV

children.label: Overview
children: Renin release (juxtaglomerular cells) → triggered by sympathetic β1 stimulation, ↓ serum Na+, ↓ GFR
Renin cleaves angiotensinogen → angiotensin I; ACE (pulmonary vascular endothelium) converts AI → AII

Angiotensin II → vasoconstriction; constricts efferent arteriole (preserves GFR when perfusion falls); ↑ proximal tubule Na+ reabsorption; ↑ aldosterone release → collecting duct Na+/fluid retention at the expense of K+

children.label: ACE Inhibitors — "-pril"
children: MOA → block AI→AII conversion; ↓ GFR (dilate efferent arteriole), ↓ PCT Na-bicarb reabsorption, ↓ aldosterone
↑ levels of AI and renin (compensatory)
Uses → 1st-line for chronic HF (↓ mortality); MI; 1st-line for HTN; slows diabetic nephropathy (start if albuminuria + BP >130/80)
↓ AII-mediated cardiac remodeling
AE → expected ↑ creatinine; significant hypotension/syncope in high-renin states (HF); hyperkalemia (↓ aldosterone)
AE → dry cough (↑ bradykinin); angioedema risk (↑ bradykinin + substance P)
Contraindicated → hereditary angioedema (C1 esterase deficiency); bilateral renal artery stenosis (precipitates renal failure — persistent ↑ creatinine)
+ NSAIDs → can precipitate AKI (afferent constriction + efferent dilation → ↓↓ GFR)
Pregnancy → risk of fetal hypotension

children.label: ARBs — "-sartan"
children: Same downstream effects as ACE inhibitors, but do NOT ↑ bradykinin (no cough/angioedema risk)
AE → hyperkalemia (↓ aldosterone)

children.label: Direct Renin Inhibitor — Aliskiren
children: MOA → prevents renin from converting AI→AII
AE → hyperkalemia

children.label: Carbonic Anhydrase Inhibitors — Acetazolamide (site: PCT)
children: MOA → inhibits carbonic anhydrase → ↓ bicarb reabsorption → bicarb stays in lumen → urine alkalinization; also natriuresis
Uses → glaucoma (↓ aqueous humor production); idiopathic intracranial hypertension (↓ CSF production); altitude/mountain sickness prophylaxis
AE → hypokalemia; type 2 (proximal) RTA; promotes calcium phosphate stones (prevents uric acid stones via alkaline urine); is a sulfa drug

children.label: Mannitol — Osmotic Diuretic (site: PCT + descending loop)
children: Uses → ↓ intracranial pressure (urgent); ↓ intraocular pressure
AE → volume expansion → pulmonary edema, can worsen heart failure; can cause hyponatremia (volume expansion) or hypernatremia (water depletion)

children.label: Loop Diuretics — Furosemide, Ethacrynic Acid (site: thick ascending limb)
children: MOA → blocks Na+/K+/2Cl– (NKCC) cotransporter — most efficacious diuretics
↓ lumen-positive potential → ↑ Mg2+ and Ca2+ excretion → chronic use → hypomagnesemia, (rare) hypocalcemia
Induces COX-2 → prostaglandins enhance salt excretion + dilate afferent arteriole (NSAIDs blunt this effect)
Uses → 1st-line for acute decompensated HF with fluid overload/pulmonary edema (↓ preload; does not prolong survival); ascites; HTN
AE → hypokalemia (can worsen arrhythmias); ototoxicity (dose-related hearing loss); interstitial nephritis; hyperuricemia (→ gout); contraction alkalosis
Most are sulfa drugs; ethacrynic acid is NOT

children.label: Thiazide Diuretics — Hydrochlorothiazide, Chlorthalidone (site: DCT)
children: MOA → blocks NaCl cotransporter on the apical membrane
↑ calcium reabsorption (proximal + distal mechanisms) → prevents calcium kidney stones; may benefit osteoporosis
Uses → 1st-line for mild-moderate HTN; symptomatic HF (loop is 1st-line for acute); nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (paradoxical ↓ polyuria via proximal volume depletion)
AE → hypercalcemia; hyperglycemia; hyperlipidemia; hyperuricemia (gout); hypokalemia; hyponatremia; ↑ serum lithium (↓ clearance); contraction alkalosis
Are sulfa drugs

children.label: K+-Sparing Diuretics — Triamterene, Amiloride, Spironolactone, Eplerenone (site: collecting duct)
children: Triamterene, Amiloride → block ENaC directly. Spironolactone, Eplerenone → antagonize the mineralocorticoid (aldosterone) receptor
Uses → 1°/2° hyperaldosteronism (Conn syndrome); heart failure (↓ mortality, prevent aldosterone-driven remodeling and K+ wasting)
Amiloride → also treats lithium-induced nephrogenic DI (blocks Li+ entry into collecting duct cells) and Liddle syndrome (overactive ENaC, with triamterene)

AE → hyperkalemia (esp. renal disease, + ACE inhibitors/beta blockers); type 4 RTA (normal anion gap acidosis + hyperkalemia — the only RTA with hyperkalemia); use a K+-wasting diuretic in these patients
Spironolactone-specific → antiandrogenic (inhibits 17α-hydroxylase, blocks androgen receptor) → gynecomastia, impotence, ↓ libido; treats PCOS hirsutism/androgen excess (after OCP trial)
Class: CA inhibitors / (acetazolamide) | Site: PCT | MOA: ↓ carbonic anhydrase | Key Electrolyte Effect: Hypokalemia, type 2 RTA | Key Use: Glaucoma, IIH, altitude sickness
Class: Mannitol | Site: PCT/desc. loop | MOA: Osmotic | Key Electrolyte Effect: Hyper- or hyponatremia | Key Use: ↓ ICP, ↓ IOP
Class: Loop / (furosemide) | Site: Thick ascending limb | MOA: Blocks NKCC | Key Electrolyte Effect: Hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia | Key Use: Acute HF / pulmonary edema
Class: Thiazides / (HCTZ) | Site: DCT | MOA: Blocks NaCl cotransporter | Key Electrolyte Effect: Hypokalemia, hypercalcemia | Key Use: HTN (1st-line), Ca2+ stones
Class: K+-sparing / (spironolactone) | Site: Collecting duct | MOA: ENaC block / aldosterone antagonism | Key Electrolyte Effect: Hyperkalemia (type 4 RTA) | Key Use: Hyperaldosteronism, HF

children.label: Overview
children: Histamine → stored in mast cell granules
H1 → Gq → allergic inflammation, ↑ nasal/bronchial mucus, ↑ vascular permeability, bronchoconstriction, sleep/arousal regulation (CNS)
H2 → Gs → gastric acid secretion

children.label: 1st-Generation H1 Blockers — Diphenhydramine, Dimenhydrinate, Chlorpheniramine, Hydroxyzine, Meclizine, Promethazine
children: Uses → type I allergic reactions (hives, allergic rhinitis) — 1st-line; motion sickness/vestibular nausea (lipophilic → enters CNS)
AE → drowsiness (crosses BBB); antimuscarinic effects (pupillary dilation, dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation, glaucoma exacerbation, delirium)
Uses → antipsychotic-induced acute dystonia (antimuscarinic effect restores dopaminergic-cholinergic balance)
AE → ↑ appetite/weight gain (antiserotonergic); dizziness/hypotension (α1 antagonism); cognitive impairment in the elderly

children.label: 2nd-Generation H1 Blockers — Fexofenadine, Cetirizine, Loratadine
children: Less lipophilic → do NOT cross BBB → less sedating, less antimuscarinic/antiserotonergic/anti-α1 effect

children.label: Overview
children: SABA (albuterol, "-terol" suffix; terbutaline, pirbuterol) → acute bronchodilation via MDI
Inhaled corticosteroids (beclomethasone, budesonide, fluticasone) → daily maintenance, anti-inflammatory; AE → oropharyngeal candidiasis

Leukotriene pathway → arachidonic acid → (lipoxygenase) → leukotrienes; LTB4 → neutrophil chemoattractant; LTC4/D4/E4 → ↑ airway permeability, mucus, bronchoconstriction (LTD4 = most potent bronchoconstrictor)
LTD4-receptor antagonists ("-kast": montelukast, zafirlukast) → oral; alternative for mild persistent asthma
Zileuton → direct lipoxygenase inhibitor → alternative for mild persistent asthma; AE → hepatotoxicity
COX inhibition shifts AA metabolism toward the LOX pathway (worsens aspirin-induced asthma)
LABA (salmeterol, formoterol) → daily controller, long duration, for moderate-severe persistent asthma
↑ ICS dose → moderate-severe persistent asthma
Methylxanthines (theophylline) → PDE inhibitor → ↑ cAMP; oral; alternative for mild-severe persistent asthma; AE → CNS stimulation (nervousness, tremor), tachycardia; metabolized by CYP450
Omalizumab → anti-IgE monoclonal antibody → prevents mast cell sensitization → adjunct for moderate-severe persistent asthma
Cromolyn sodium → inhibits mast cell degranulation → prevents histamine release

children.label: Acute Severe Exacerbation
children: Inhaled SABA (albuterol)
Systemic corticosteroids (IV or oral)
Nebulized ipratropium bromide (anticholinergic)
SC/IM epinephrine
Class: SABA | Example(s): Albuterol, terbutaline | Role: Acute relief
Class: LABA | Example(s): Salmeterol, formoterol | Role: Daily controller (moderate-severe)
Class: ICS | Example(s): Beclomethasone, budesonide, fluticasone | Role: Daily maintenance; AE: oral candidiasis
Class: LTD4 antagonists | Example(s): Montelukast, zafirlukast | Role: Oral; mild persistent
Class: LOX inhibitor | Example(s): Zileuton | Role: Mild persistent; hepatotoxic
Class: Methylxanthines | Example(s): Theophylline | Role: Mild-severe; CNS/cardiac AE
Class: Anti-IgE | Example(s): Omalizumab | Role: Adjunct, moderate-severe
Class: Mast cell stabilizer | Example(s): Cromolyn sodium | Role: Prevents degranulation

children.label: Overview
children: Alprostadil (PGE1) → vasodilator; maintains PDA patency; treats erectile dysfunction (NSAIDs/indomethacin close the PDA — opposite effect)
Misoprostol (PGE1) → ↑ protective gastric mucus → prevents NSAID-induced ulcers; also induces labor/terminates pregnancy; AE → diarrhea
Dinoprostone (PGE2) → uterine contraction + cervical ripening → labor induction/pregnancy termination
Carboprost (PGF2α) → uterine contraction → controls postpartum hemorrhage / pregnancy termination
Latanoprost, Travoprost (PGF2α) → ↑ aqueous humor outflow → treat glaucoma; AE → brown iris pigmentation
Iloprost, Epoprostenol (prostacyclin analogs) → vasodilation → treat pulmonary HTN (IV epoprostenol = 1st-line, improves symptoms/survival, delays transplant); AE → flushing, headache, hypotension
PDE-5 inhibitors ("-afil": sildenafil, tadalafil) → ↑ cGMP → myosin light chain dephosphorylation → smooth muscle relaxation → treat pulmonary HTN and erectile dysfunction
Bosentan → endothelin receptor antagonist → vasodilation → treats pulmonary HTN; AE → fatal hepatotoxicity
Type: PGE1 | Drug(s): Alprostadil | Use: Maintain PDA; erectile dysfunction
Type: PGE1 | Drug(s): Misoprostol | Use: Prevent NSAID ulcers; labor induction/termination
Type: PGE2 | Drug(s): Dinoprostone | Use: Labor induction/termination (cervical ripening)
Type: PGF2α | Drug(s): Carboprost | Use: Postpartum hemorrhage; pregnancy termination
Type: PGF2α | Drug(s): Latanoprost, Travoprost | Use: Glaucoma (↑ outflow); brown iris pigmentation
Type: PGI2 analog | Drug(s): Iloprost, Epoprostenol | Use: Pulmonary HTN
